content.prompt: A model rocket is launched into the air. Its height after $t$ seconds is given by $h(t)=-t^2+10t$, where $h$ is in metres.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the average rate of change of height between $t=0$ and $t=4$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Average rate of change}&=\frac{h(4)-h(0)}{4-0}\\&=\frac{(-4^2+10\times4)-0}{4}\\&=\frac{24}{4}\\&=6\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked: The ball was thrown at $t=0$, so find $h(0)$, its initial height in metres.

children.label: b
children.prompt: At what rate was the height changing 20 seconds after being thrown?

children.label: c
children.prompt: When was the ball at maximum height?

answer.short: Solve $h'(t)=0$ for the time at maximum height.
answer.worked: Solve $h'(t)=0$. Choose the time when the height changes from increasing to decreasing; this is the time of maximum height.

answer.worked: Increasing height has a positive rate, so solve $h'(t)=20$ for the time in seconds.

children.label: f

content.prompt:
An infestation of ants hit a Year 7’s locker but was gradually brought under control.

The ant population $P$, in hundreds, $t$ hours after it was discovered, is $P(t)=7+6t-t^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the initial population of the ants.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(0)&=7+6(0)-(0)^2\\&=7\text{ hundred ants}\end{align*}$$
The initial population was $700$ ants.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the initial rate at which the population was changing.

answer.short: $6$ hundred ants per hour ($600$ ants per hour), increasing.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P'(t)&=6-2t\\P'(0)&=6-2(0)\\&=6\text{ hundred ants per hour}\end{align*}$$
Initially, the population was increasing by $600$ ants per hour.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the ant population is changing after 4 hours.

answer.short: $-2$ hundred ants per hour; decreasing by $200$ ants per hour.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P'(t)&=6-2t\\P'(4)&=6-2(4)\\&=-2\text{ hundred ants per hour}\end{align*}$$
After $4$ hours, the population was decreasing by $200$ ants per hour.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find when the ant population was at its maximum.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P'(t)&=0\\6-2t&=0\\t&=3\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$
The quadratic opens downwards, so this stationary point is a maximum.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the maximum population of the ants.

answer.worked:
The maximum occurs at $t=3$ hours.
$$\begin{align*}P(3)&=7+6(3)-3^2\\&=16\text{ hundred ants}\end{align*}$$
The maximum population was $1600$ ants.

children.label: f
children.prompt: When were the ants finally eliminated?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(t)&=0\\7+6t-t^2&=0\\t^2-6t-7&=0\\(t-7)(t+1)&=0\\t&=-1\text{ or }7\end{align*}$$
Reject $t=-1$ because time is measured after discovery. The ants were eliminated after $7$ hours.

answer.worked:
Using the quotient rule:
$$\begin{align*}V'(t)&=\frac{-1(2+t)-(10-t)(1)}{(2+t)^2}\\V'(t)&=\frac{-2-t-10+t}{(2+t)^2}\\V'(t)&=-\frac{12}{(2+t)^2}\end{align*}$$

answer.short: $V'(t)<0$ throughout the physical model, so the volume is decreasing.
answer.worked: For $0\le t\le10$, $(2+t)^2>0$, so $V'(t)=-\dfrac{12}{(2+t)^2}<0$. Therefore the container loses water throughout the model, until it is empty.

content.prompt: The rate of water flow into a tank is given by $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=10(2-t)$, where $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$ is measured in litres per minute. The tank initially had 60 litres of water in it.

children.prompt:

answer.short: At $t=1$, water flows into the tank at $10$ L/min. At $t=4$, water flows out at $20$ L/min.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\left.\frac{dV}{dt}\right|_{t=1}&=10(2-1)\\&=10\text{ L/min}\\\left.\frac{dV}{dt}\right|_{t=4}&=10(2-4)\\&=-20\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$$
The positive rate at $t=1$ means water flows into the tank at $10$ L/min. The negative rate at $t=4$ means water flows out at $20$ L/min.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the volume of water increases for a certain amount of time, and then decreases afterwards.

answer.short: The volume increases for the first $2$ minutes, then decreases, since $\dfrac{dV}{dt}>0$ for $0\le t<2$ and $\dfrac{dV}{dt}<0$ for $t>2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dV}{dt}&=10(2-t)\\10(2-t)&=0\\t&=2\end{align*}$$
For $0\le t<2$, $10(2-t)>0$, so the volume is increasing. At $t=2$, the rate is zero. For $t>2$, $10(2-t)<0$, so the volume is decreasing.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dV}{dt}&=20-10t\\&=10(2-t)\\V(0)&=20(0)-5(0)^2+60\\&=60\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
The formula gives the stated flow rate and the initial volume of $60$ litres.

children.prompt: Find the time taken for all the ice to melt.

$$\begin{align*}0&=8-\frac{t^2}{32}\\t^2&=256\\t&=16\end{align*}$$
Time is non-negative, so all the ice melts after 16 minutes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the ice is melting after 4 minutes.

answer.short: $-0.25\text{ kg/min}$; the mass decreases by $0.25\text{ kg/min}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dM}{dt}&=-\frac{t}{16}\\\left.\frac{dM}{dt}\right|_{t=4}&=-\frac{4}{16}\\&=-0.25\text{ kg/min}\end{align*}$$
The mass is decreasing by $0.25\text{ kg/min}$.

children.prompt: Find the rate at which the ice is melting when 2 kg of ice has melted.

When 2 kg has melted, $M=8-2=6$ kg.

children.prompt: What was the share price after one year?

The share price was $\$5.60$.

The share price was increasing at $\$2.40$ per year.

children.prompt: Find when the share price was stationary.

content.prompt: A cricket ball is thrown vertically upwards. Its height $x$ in metres at time $t$ seconds after it is thrown is given by $x=20t-5t^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find $v$ and $a$ as functions of $t$, and show that the ball is always accelerating downwards. Then sketch graphs of $x$, $v$ and $a$ against $t$.

answer.short: $x=5t(4-t)$, $v=20-10t\text{ m/s}$ and $a=-10\text{ m/s}^2$. The acceleration is always downwards. Graphs are shown for $0\le t\le4$.
answer.worked:
Taking upwards as positive,
$$\begin{align*}v(t)&=\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=20-10t,\\a(t)&=\frac{dv}{dt}\\&=-10.\end{align*}$$
Thus the acceleration is $10\text{ m/s}^2$ downwards throughout the flight.
$$\begin{align*}x(t)&=20t-5t^2\\&=5t(4-t).\end{align*}$$
The height graph crosses the time axis at $t=0$ and $t=4$, with maximum $(2,20)$. The velocity graph joins $(0,20)$ to $(4,-20)$ and crosses the time axis at $t=2$. The acceleration graph is horizontal at $a=-10$.

spec.description: Three complete native solution graphs in reading order: height above, velocity then acceleration below; all original paths, values, guides and labels retained.
spec.mathematics: For 0≤t≤4: x=20t−5t², vertex (2,20); v=20−10t, intercepts (0,20), (2,0), endpoint (4,−20); a=−10.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no supplied graph appears in the student prompt.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the speed at which the ball was thrown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}v(0)&=20-10(0)\\&=20\text{ m/s}.\end{align*}$$
The initial speed is $|v(0)|=20\text{ m/s}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find when it returns to the ground (that is, when $x=0$) and show that its speed then is equal to the initial speed.

answer.short: It returns after $4\text{ s}$. Its speed then is $20\text{ m/s}$, equal to its initial speed.
answer.worked:
$$5t(4-t)=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=0\text{ or }4.$$
The return occurs at $t=4\text{ s}$, since $t=0$ is the launch.
$$v(4)=20-10(4)=-20\text{ m/s},\qquad |v(4)|=20\text{ m/s}=|v(0)|.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find its maximum height above the ground and the time taken to reach this height.

answer.worked:
At the maximum height, $v=0$.
$$20-10t=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=2\text{ s}.$$
$$x(2)=20(2)-5(2)^2=20\text{ m}.$$
Since $a=-10<0$, this stationary height is a maximum.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the acceleration at the top of the flight, and explain why the acceleration can be non-zero when the ball is stationary.

answer.short: $-10\text{ m/s}^2$. The velocity is zero for an instant but is still changing.
answer.worked: $a(2)=-10\text{ m/s}^2$, or $10\text{ m/s}^2$ downwards. At the top, $v(2)=0$, but the velocity continues to decrease from positive to negative. Acceleration measures the rate of change of velocity, so it remains non-zero at that instant.
